comparisons.peer_topic: CCAR stress testing process and outcomes
comparisons.peer_summary: The Federal Reserve conducts annual CCAR stress tests using hypothetical economic scenarios that may affect the Company's SCB levels, as evidenced by the 2024 increase in the SCB result.
comparisons.comparison: The target (Citi) discloses the results of its specific annual goodwill impairment test, confirming no impairment occurred and that fair value exceeded carrying value for all reporting units. In contrast, the peer (BAC) discusses the regulatory CCAR stress testing process and the determination of the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB). While both disclosures relate to capital adequacy and asset valuation assessments, they address fundamentally different mechanisms: Citi reports the outcome of an internal accounting impairment test on goodwill assets, whereas BAC describes the external regulatory stress testing framework that influences its capital buffer requirements.

sentences.text: Citi performed its annual goodwill impairment test, which resulted in no impairment of any of Citi's reporting units' goodwill.
For each of the Company's reporting units, fair value exceeded carrying value by at least 10%.
As part of its CCAR, the Federal Reserve conducts stress testing on parts of our business using hypothetical economic scenarios prepared by the Federal Reserve.
Those scenarios may affect our CCAR stress test results, which may impact the level of our SCB.

comparisons.peer_topic: CCAR Stress Testing and SCB Requirements
comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorgan Chase is subject to annual supervisory stress tests under the CCAR framework and must submit an annual capital plan, with the Federal Reserve using severely adverse scenario results to determine the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB); the firm is required to file its 2025 CCAR submission by April 5, 2025, with final SCB requirements effective October 1, 2025, amid pending changes to the framework and legal challenges.
comparisons.comparison: The target (Citi) details the results of its annual goodwill impairment test, stating no impairment occurred and fair value exceeded carrying value for each reporting unit. The peer (JPM) discusses its obligations under the CCAR framework and supervisory stress tests, specifically how the Federal Reserve uses these results to determine the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB). While both involve annual assessments of financial health and capital, Citi's disclosure is an accounting result of an internal goodwill test, whereas JPM's is a description of regulatory capital planning and stress test methodologies affecting regulatory buffers.

sentences.text: For each of the Company's reporting units, fair value exceeded carrying value by at least 10%.

As a large BHC, JPMorganChase is subject to supervisory stress testing administered by the Federal Reserve as part of the Federal Reserve's annual Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review ("CCAR") framework.

The Federal Reserve uses the results under the severely adverse scenario from its supervisory stress test to determine the Firm's Stress Capital Buffer ("SCB") requirement for the coming year, which forms part of the Firm's applicable capital buffers.
